chunks: Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Qiyama al-Wasiti, who said:

I entered upon Ali ibn Musa (عليه السلام), and I said to him: “Can there be two Imams?” He said: “No, except that one of them is silent.” So I said to him: “Here you are; there is no silent one for you,” and Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) had not yet been born to him. So he said to me: “By Allah, Allah will surely bring forth from me that by which He will establish the truth and its people, and erase falsehood and its people.”
Then after a year, Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) was born to him, and Ibn Qiyama was a Waqifi.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja‘far, referring here to Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (عليه السلام)
key_terms.إِمَامَانِ: two Imams existing in the context of succession and divine authority
key_terms.الْبَاطِلَ: falsehood, meaning the invalid cause and its adherents
key_terms.الْحَقَّ: the truth, meaning the true divine cause and its rightful adherents
key_terms.صَامِتٌ: silent; an Imam who does not outwardly exercise active leadership alongside another Imam
key_terms.وَاقِفِيًّا: a member of the Waqifi sect, which halted at a previous Imam and denied the continuation of the Imamate

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the designation of Imam Abu Ja‘far al-Jawad (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a question posed to Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (عليه السلام) about whether two Imams can exist at once. He explains that this only occurs when one of them is silent, then foretells the birth of Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), through whom the truth would be established and falsehood effaced. The report is significant in discussions of the continuity of the Imamate and the refutation of Waqifi doubts.
